content.jointProblem: Which firmware architecture and hybrid classical/post-quantum signing flow could support ML-DSA in the KL-HSM line within its memory, performance and security constraints? The first experiment would port a standards-conformant ML-DSA implementation to representative KL-HSM hardware and its production toolchain, testing correctness, memory use, signing latency and leakage before using the findings to develop a versioned migration roadmap and integration proof of concept.

rationale.text: Nikolić has direct experience implementing and measuring Dilithium signatures on ARM Cortex-M hardware, relevant to evaluating the company's ML-DSA migration.

sources.quote: We implement the NIST post-quantum signature finalists CRYSTALS-Dilithium (security levels 2 and 3) and Falcon-512 in C
Signing is substantially more expensive for Falcon due to the discrete Gaussian sampler: 14.8 ms versus 3.2 ms for Dilithium-2.

rationale.text: Her HSM project experience combines algorithm adaptation, implementation security evaluation and migration-roadmap work.

sources.quote: Work packages cover algorithm selection and adaptation, FPGA and secure microcontroller implementation, side-channel and fault-injection evaluation, and a migration roadmap document targeting IEC 62443 compliance.

rationale.text: Her work supports testing implementation security under the actual compiler and architecture rather than assuming that nominally constant-time source code is sufficient.

sources.quote: Leakage detection using Welch's t-test and TVLA methodology crosses the threshold of |t| = 4.5 in three of eight compiler/architecture combinations.
We trace each instance to specific compiler transformations visible in the generated assembly

rationale.text: She has developed reproducible embedded-PQC benchmarking methods suitable for structuring performance and resource trade-off measurements.

sources.quote: We validate the suite by collecting results for Kyber-512, Dilithium-2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and Classic McEliece 348864 across all four targets.
a fixed GCC toolchain version and flag set, a cycle-counting harness based on hardware performance counters

rationale.text: She brings industrial PQC-readiness assessment experience and has explicitly expressed interest in joint projects with HSM developers.

sources.quote: a six-month applied research contract in 2022 covering PQC readiness assessment for their smart metering gateway product line.
joint projects with companies developing HSMs, IoT security firmware, or industrial control system security

constraints.text: The proof of concept must fit the KL-HSM's actual flash and RAM limits and integrate with its existing ARM Cortex-M C firmware; a drop-in replacement cannot be assumed.

sources.quote: Our HSM firmware runs on a constrained microcontroller with limited flash and RAM, so a straight drop-in is not possible.
Custom ARM Cortex-M firmware in C for HSM cryptographic operations

constraints.text: The migration must address larger key material, changed signature flows, hybrid operation and the product's PKCS#11 interface, rather than delivering an isolated algorithm benchmark.

sources.quote: we have not touched the firmware architecture to accommodate larger key material or different signature flows.
how hybrid classical/post-quantum operation will work during transition.
PKCS#11 and RFC 5280 / RFC 6960 (OCSP) standards

constraints.text: The plan must account for the KL-500's stated Common Criteria EAL4+ certification objective when proposing firmware changes; the current certification status needs confirmation.

sources.quote: Kriptolog intends to achieve Common Criteria EAL4+ certification for the KL-500 HSM by the end of 2025

constraints.text: Scope must support a documented roadmap and at least one working integration proof of concept within twelve months, including firmware-version planning and measured performance trade-offs.

sources.quote: A good outcome is a documented roadmap and at least one working proof-of-concept integration inside twelve months.
which firmware version will support post-quantum algorithms, what the performance trade-offs are

constraints.text: The company work package must remain well-defined and practically applicable within its modest collaborative R&D capacity.

sources.quote: with modest capacity to take on collaborative projects if the scope is well-defined and the output is practically applicable.

constraints.text: Work should include real hardware and measurable deliverables. If SLE97 comparison hardware is needed, laboratory access must accommodate the limit of two evaluation kits or partner-supplied units.

sources.quote: Prefers collaborative arrangements that involve real hardware and measurable deliverables rather than purely theoretical work.
The lab has limited availability of the Infineon SLE97 evaluation kits (two units); industrial partners providing additional hardware would accelerate shared projects.

risks: Published Dilithium results use an STM32F407 and earlier scheme variants, not the KL-HSM production platform or necessarily final ML-DSA. The initial target-hardware experiment must establish correctness, resource fit and security under the company's toolchain; published timings are not forecasts.

The demonstrated hybrid HSM architecture combines ECDH and Kyber using a secure microcontroller plus FPGA. It does not validate hybrid RSA/ECDSA and ML-DSA signing on the company's constrained microcontroller; prototype the signing policy, interface and verifier compatibility separately.
Memory optimisation and acceptable latency may conflict with side-channel or fault resistance. Successful functional integration would not establish production security or certification readiness.

The researcher's current availability is unknown. Company engineering allocation, project budget, hardware access and acceptance thresholds are also unspecified, threatening the twelve-month schedule.
The stated end-2025 certification target does not establish current certification status. Firmware changes could require additional evaluation work whose scope and cost are unknown.
Client verifier capabilities and transition requirements are unspecified; a working HSM implementation alone may not produce an interoperable migration path.
questions: Can Nikolić commit to the proposed twelve-month joint project, and what researcher and laboratory effort is available?
Which KL-300 or KL-500 variant is the initial target, and what are its exact MCU, free flash/RAM, compiler, RTOS, acceleration features and firmware-access arrangements?
Will Kriptolog provide representative development HSMs, firmware source, build tools, its existing ML-DSA prototype and non-production test keys?
Does the scope cover client firmware signing, verification of the HSM's own updates, or both? Which ML-DSA parameter sets, latency, throughput and memory thresholds define acceptance?
What does hybrid signing mean for these clients: dual signatures, separate selectable mechanisms, or another construction? Which PKCS#11 consumers and firmware verifiers must interoperate?
What is the KL-500's current Common Criteria status, and which evaluator-approved change-control, side-channel and fault-testing requirements apply?
What budget and named company engineering allocation are available, and which firmware release milestones must the roadmap support?
What confidentiality, publication, intellectual-property and library-licensing terms will govern access to proprietary firmware and delivery of the proof of concept?
